findings.text: Symbol __pi_memset provides a position independent memory set service that fills a byte range with a repeated byte value and returns the original destination address. The fragment selects between a generic routine and a hardware memory operation sequence gated by a processor feature alternative.

Internal helper __pi_memset_generic accepts a destination with a length and a fill value under the same contract as the public entry and preserves the incoming destination for return. It handles all lengths including zero and small sizes without requiring prior alignment from the caller.

The generic fill distinguishes small ranges with medium ranges and large ranges plus a dedicated zero path. Small ranges complete with narrowing stores, larger ranges move to an aligned steady state with wide paired stores and a cache aligned bulk loop, and zero requests may switch to line zeroing when size and hardware support allow, otherwise rejoining the fill steady state.

Fill values are reduced to the low byte and replicated across wider store units so every byte of the requested range receives the same pattern. The routine maintains destination progress and remaining length as complementary quantities and guarantees exactly the requested span is updated apart from benign repeated coverage in some tails.

Size selection treats sixteen bytes as the split between narrow completion and aligned wide progress, uses sixty four byte units for bulk steady work under a sixty four byte line assumption, and gates hardware line zeroing behind sixty three byte and one hundred twenty eight byte minima.

Symbol mte_zero_clear_page_tags zeroes one page of memory while clearing associated allocation tags. It normalizes the incoming address to tag free form and processes a full page stride before returning.
Symbol mte_copy_page_tags copies allocation tags from a source page to a destination page over a full page stride, advancing both pointers by a transfer granularity supplied by platform helpers.

Tag zeroing prefers a hardware granule zero path when a system register indicates it is permitted and derives the step from a size field, otherwise it falls back to a tag setting store loop. Tag copying uses paired tag load and store operations and terminates on page boundary wrap.

Symbol __pi_strchr searches a NUL terminated byte string for the low byte of a character argument and returns a pointer to the first match or a null pointer when the terminator is reached first, including correct handling when searching for the terminator itself.

Symbol __pi_strrchr scans a NUL terminated byte string and returns a pointer to the last occurrence of the low byte of a character argument, or a null pointer when absent, by retaining the most recent match until the terminator.

Symbol __pi_strcmp performs unsigned byte lexicographic comparison of two NUL terminated strings and returns a negative or zero or positive result reflecting the first differing byte or equal termination. It supports mutually aligned with misaligned and initially unaligned inputs and accounts for byte order differences.

Symbol __pi_strncmp compares at most a bounded number of bytes from two possibly unterminated buffers with unsigned byte semantics, returning zero when the bound is zero or when the compared prefix matches including early joint termination, otherwise a signed difference of the first differing bytes.

Symbol __pi_strlen returns the number of bytes before the first NUL in a NUL terminated string. It avoids crossing into an unreadable page near the end of a page and uses wide word checks with distinct fast and precise phases for ASCII heavy and non ASCII data.

Symbol __pi_strnlen returns the smaller of a supplied bound and the length before the first NUL, returning the bound itself when no NUL appears within it or when the bound is zero. It tolerates arbitrarily misaligned starts by masking leading bytes outside the string.

Symbol __ashlti3 implements logical left shift of a one hundred twenty eight bit integer value presented as a low and high word pair by a bit count, returning the shifted pair with low bits filled with zero and high bits carried from the low word.

Symbol __ashrti3 implements arithmetic right shift of a one hundred twenty eight bit integer value presented as a low and high word pair by a bit count, propagating the original sign into vacated high bits and carrying high word bits into the low word.

Both one hundred twenty eight bit shifts leave the operand unchanged for a zero count and switch behavior around a word width boundary, with large counts producing results derived only from one input word plus sign or zero fill rather than combining both words.

Length and comparison routines detect NUL bytes and differences with word parallel arithmetic that combines subtraction with masking and bit testing across all bytes of a register, refined by position extraction through leading zero counting to order the first significant byte.

Several memory and string paths trade exact store coverage or speculative wide loads for speed by rewriting some tail bytes with unaligned paired accesses or pre rounding addresses with masking. Correctness depends on those extra accesses staying within mapped and writable memory and on callers never relying on untouched bytes beyond the requested span.

Observed memory facts center on MTE_TAG_SHIFT with PAGE_SIZE and MTE_GRANULE_SIZE for tag math and page stride, on dczid_el0 for probing line zero permission and block size, on L1_CACHE_SHIFT for loop alignment, and on ARM64_HAS_MOPS for selecting the accelerated fill path.

Observed string facts center on REP8_01 with REP8_7f for parallel terminator sensing, on REP8_80 for masking forced bits, on MIN_PAGE_SIZE for page boundary guarding, and on __AARCH64EB__ for endian specific adjustment.
